stem: You examine Lotta. She has percussion and palpation tenderness in the right iliac fossa, which is aggravated when you make her jump. She is febrile at 38ºC and is flushed in the face. Which of the following clinical signs would be UNLIKELY to suggest peritonitis/perforation?
explanation: Peritonitis or perforation typically causes abdominal guarding/rigidity, tenderness, and reduced bowel sounds. Increased bowel sounds are less suggestive and may be seen early or with other non-peritoneal processes.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Abdominal pain

rationale: The question asks for the sign least likely to suggest peritonitis/perforation. Increased bowel sounds best fits that description.

optionExplanations.A: A hard or rigid abdomen suggests guarding and peritoneal irritation.
optionExplanations.B: Vomiting is common in appendicitis and can occur with peritonitis, so it is not unlikely.
optionExplanations.C: Increased bowel sounds are not a typical sign of peritonitis/perforation; bowel sounds are more often reduced or absent.
optionExplanations.E: Pain with movement or abdominal wall contraction can indicate peritoneal irritation.
